source: JZ Mock A · Paper 1 · Question 10 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Differentiate fractional powers and retain a sign-changing denominator

hints.title: Rewrite as powers
hints.body: Express both cube-root terms using rational exponents before differentiating term by term.
hints.recap: The power rule applies to rational powers on their real domain.
hints.pitfall: A reciprocal cube root contributes a negative exponent.

recall.reminder: The power rule applies to rational powers on their real domain.

hints.title: Keep domain breaks in the sign table
hints.body: Mark both numerator zeros and excluded inputs. Check the sign of every remaining factor on each interval.
hints.recap: A derivative sign table must include domain breaks as well as stationary points.
hints.pitfall: An odd-root power of a negative input can be negative; do not cancel its sign from an inequality.
hints.pause: Select the intervals with nonnegative derivative and check their endpoints.

recall.reminder: A derivative sign table must include domain breaks as well as stationary points.

solution:
1. Write f(x)=14x4/3+x1/3+3x−2/3, with x≠0. The real cube-root powers are valid for negative inputs too.

2. Then f′(x)=13x1/3+13x−2/3−2x−5/3=(x+3)(x−2)3x5/3.

3. The numerator changes sign at −3 and 2; the denominator has the sign of x. The derivative signs on (−∞,−3), (−3,0), (0,2) and (2,∞) are respectively −,+,−,+.

4. The stated convention includes the zero-derivative endpoints −3 and 2, but the function excludes 0. Therefore −3≤x<0 or x≥2. Answer A.
